label: Tower value separation
query: How should Tower separate value-at-stake, committed value, measuring value, and realized savings for the Kyriba program?
answer: My read for Lakeshore Holdings: For Kyriba (LSH-KYRIBA-TREASURY-2026), Tower should treat value as a funnel: broad “value-at-stake” at the top, with progressively tighter, evidence-backed subsets for “committed value,” “measured value,” and finally “realized savings.” Each tier needs its own owner, artifact, and gate so you don’t overstate impact or double-count. Why (anchored in Kyriba’s current spine and Lakeshore context) You have Strategy through BAFO approved for Kyriba, but Executive Decision, Selection, Transition, and Value are still in review. That means the “value” story must be clearly staged, not presented as done. Treasury programs like Kyriba typically have multi-bucket value (FX, liquidity, working capital, controls). Without explicit separation, teams mix aspiration with signed-off savings and erode credibility with Finance. Tower’s job is comparability across Moves — the same value definitions have to work for AMS modernization, data work, etc., not just Kyriba. How I’d define each tier for Kyriba in Tower 1) Value-at-stake (VAS) – “total plausible upside” Definition: The full, defensible opportunity range if Kyriba is perfectly adopted across scope (e.g., all entities, all cash pools, all in-scope bank accounts). Examples for Kyriba: Potential working-capital release from better cash visibility and forecasting. Avoidable bank fees and transaction costs. Risk loss-avoidance from stronger controls (fraud, payment errors, FX mishandling). Tower treatment: Sits in Strategy/Concept artifacts and is tagged as “VAS – not committed.” Range-based (low/med/high) with clear assumptions (e.g., “assumes 100% of bank accounts onboarded by Year 2”).
